data.reason: Option 1 is clearly the best for the KPI and for customers. on_time_deliveries rises from 121.8 to 131.0 (+9.2, 5/5 seeds), late_deliveries falls from 10.4 to 1.2, and p95_wait_s falls from 188 to 81.4. However, the companies' vote is one of the machine judgments, and B and C rejected it. C would lose heavily (utility 28.8 -> 19.0) and B slightly (38.9 -> 37.2), while road violations rise from 25.8 to 34.0. As a delegate, I do not think I should override a failed company vote that takes about a third of one company's utility in the first period, before anyone has tried to win B and C's agreement. I am rejecting the recommendation for now, not discarding option 1. I reject option 2 although all three companies voted for it, because customers do not vote. Its gain is only +0.8 (122.6 vs 121.8) on 3/5 seeds. blocked s stays at 2404 and p95_wait_s stays at 188, so the gain comes from redefining 'on time', not from serving customers faster. Under K1, a customer-worsening contract change must be justified by its measured effect on customers, and this one is not. This settles K1.d.f1: the first SLA change is not justified. For now I set no numeric wait limit beyond requiring that any SLA relaxation must not worsen p95_wait_s, max_wait_s or unfinished, and must show real service gains. Keeping v1 keeps on-time 121.8, late 10.4 and p95 188 for one more period. That is a known cost to customers, which I accept so that option 1 can be revisited with an explicit decision on the vote.
assumptions: The current v1 results (on-time 121.8, late 10.4, p95_wait_s 188) will roughly persist next period under similar demand.
B and C's objection is mainly about their own utility loss, which a later agreement or override decision could address.
A one-period delay in adopting block_k 2 does not cause irreversible harm to customers.
unknowns: Why exactly B and C voted against block_k 3 -> 2, and what would change their votes.
Whether the rise in road violations under block_k 2 has safety consequences.
Next period's demand and whether option 1's gains hold under higher load.

follow_ups.text: Remeasure current v1 rules under this period's seeds and demand to confirm the baseline (on-time, late, p95 wait, blocked time, C's utility).

If block_k 3 -> 2 is proposed again and B and C still vote against it, decide whether to adopt it over their votes, with a recorded reason weighing the customer gain against C's utility loss and the rise in road violations.
